documents.title: Guidance for Faculty & Students
documents.stance_why: The provost page sets no single rule; it says instructors decide, "make explicit in their syllabi and assignment descriptions which uses of Gen-AI are permitted in coursework, if any, and which are prohibited". That hands the decision to instructors.
documents.summary: Provost FAQs for faculty and students on appropriate Gen-AI use. They hand the AI rule to instructors and syllabi, advise on discussing and designing around AI, protect privacy and student IP, discourage detectors and AI grading, and set disclosure and honor-code expectations for students.

documents.title: Setting Boundaries for AI Use Through Syllabus Statements
documents.stance_why: The collection offers example statements from several instructors, from prohibition to required use, and says instructors "set and communicate boundaries" themselves, so it sets no stance and delegates.

documents.title: AI Policy (student use of AI tools in Data Science courses)
documents.stance_why: The school policy requires syllabi to state AI rules but sets a default when silent: AI "is permitted with the following activities... at no penalty", with drafting and sentence-writing banned and the closing line "the use of foundation models is encouraged". Permission with conditions fits better than delegates because a concrete baseline applies.
documents.summary: The School of Data Science policy requires every syllabus to state allowable AI uses, lists student rights and responsibilities, and sets default rules when a syllabus is silent: permitted idea, outline and grammar uses, banned drafting, required citation, and a zero for violations.
